title: Meta Is Cutting 8,000 Jobs Tomorrow and Shifting 7,000 Into AI. For Indian Tech Workers, the Clock Is Ticking.
excerpt: The largest Big Tech layoff of 2026 begins Wednesday. H-1B holders have 60 days to find a new sponsor — or leave the country.
body:
Meta will cut approximately 8,000 jobs beginning Wednesday, May 20 — roughly ten per cent of its global workforce — while simultaneously reassigning 7,000 employees into artificial intelligence roles, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. It is the company's largest single round of layoffs since the "Year of Efficiency" purge of 2022-23, and it lands squarely on the desks of thousands of Indian-origin engineers, product managers and data scientists who form a substantial share of Meta's technical ranks.

## The Memo and the Math

The restructuring plan, outlined by Meta's Chief People Officer Janelle Gale in a memo circulated to staff on Monday, calls for flattening management layers and rebuilding teams around what the company describes as "AI-native design principles." Affected employees worldwide will receive formal notifications in three batches starting at 4 AM local time on Wednesday. A further 6,000 open positions will be cancelled outright.

Gale wrote that many organisational leaders had already incorporated AI-native structures into their plans. "We're now at the stage where many orgs can operate with a flatter structure with smaller teams of pods/cohorts that can move faster and with more ownership," the memo stated. Meta declined to comment publicly.

The financial context is staggering. Meta reported a 33 per cent revenue increase in the first quarter of 2026, yet CEO Mark Zuckerberg has signalled that up to $135 billion in annual capital expenditure will be directed toward AI infrastructure — a bet on what he has called "personal super intelligence" for the platform's 3.9 billion monthly active users. The layoffs are not a distress signal; they are a reallocation.

## The Indian Workforce in the Crosshairs

No official breakdown of affected employees by nationality has been released, but the implications for the Indian tech diaspora are unmistakable. Indians and Indian Americans constitute one of the largest demographic groups in Silicon Valley's engineering workforce. H-1B visa holders face a particularly precarious position: under current US immigration rules, a laid-off worker on an H-1B has 60 days to find a new employer willing to sponsor them, or they must leave the country.

Immigration attorneys across the Bay Area are already bracing for a wave of consultations. For those on employment-based green card tracks — where Indian nationals face backlogs stretching decades — a sudden job loss can reset years of waiting.

The anxiety extends beyond those directly affected. Over 1,000 Meta employees recently signed an internal petition opposing a newly deployed mouse-tracking software that monitors desktop activity, reportedly to train AI models that replicate human-computer interactions. The tool has become a lightning rod for broader frustrations about surveillance, autonomy and the uneasy feeling that the machines being built may eventually replace the people building them.

## A Sector-Wide Tremor

Meta is not acting alone. Global tech layoffs have already exceeded 80,000 in the first quarter of 2026, with Oracle leading the tally at 25,000 cuts. The pattern is consistent: companies are posting record revenues while simultaneously shrinking headcounts, redirecting the savings into AI compute, data centres and model training.

For the roughly 300,000 Indian IT professionals working in the United States on temporary visas, the message is unsettling. The roles most vulnerable to AI-driven consolidation — quality assurance, manual testing, mid-level project management, routine data analysis — overlap significantly with the positions that have historically served as entry points for immigrant tech workers.

## What It Means for NRIs

The ripple effects will be felt well beyond Menlo Park. Families in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Pune who invested heavily in their children's American tech careers are watching nervously. Remittances from the US tech sector contribute meaningfully to household incomes back home, and any sustained contraction in hiring will eventually show up in those flows.

For current employees who survive this round, the restructuring offers a different kind of pressure: the expectation to pivot into AI roles regardless of prior expertise. Meta's CTO Andrew Bosworth recently issued what employees described as a "performance ultimatum," declaring that underperformance is "not an option" in the new structure.

The era of comfortable tech employment — generous perks, predictable promotions, and the quiet understanding that large companies rarely fire engineers — is ending. In its place is something leaner, faster and far less forgiving. For the Indian diaspora, which built much of its American dream on the stability of Big Tech, Wednesday's notifications will be a wake-up call.
